content.problemStatement: With two strings `s` (the input) and `p` (the pattern), determine whether the pattern `p` matches the entire string `s`. The pattern `p` may contain lowercase letters, the wildcard `.` (which matches exactly one character), and `*` (which matches zero or more occurrences of the immediately preceding element). The match must cover the whole string `s` (not a substring). Every `*` in `p` is guaranteed to have a valid preceding element.
constraints: s contains only lowercase English letters (a-z).
p contains only lowercase English letters (a-z), '.' and '*'.
Every '*' has a valid preceding element.
content.inputFormat: Single line: JSON array of arguments: [s, p]. Example: ["aa","a*"]
content.outputFormat: Single line: JSON-serialised boolean (true or false). Example: true
notes: The pattern must match the entire string s (full-string match).
The '.' character matches exactly one arbitrary character.
The '*' character modifies the immediately preceding element and matches zero or more occurrences of that element.
Indexing is 0-based when reasoning about characters; implementations should avoid off-by-one errors when accessing p[j+1].
Empty string and empty pattern cases: an empty pattern matches only an empty string; patterns composed entirely of x* groups (for example "a*b*c*") can match an empty string.

sampleTestCases.explanation: Pattern "a" matches exactly one 'a' while the input has two characters; full-string match fails.
The token "a*" can match zero or more 'a' characters; it matches both characters in "aa".
"." matches any single character and "*" allows repetition; ".*" can match the entire string "ab".

hidden.label: Edge: single char vs star pattern
Star-heavy pattern with no terminal match

notes: All hidden test cases are concrete and use the documented JSON argument format.
The checker compares the returned boolean value (true or false).
Expected outputs are unambiguous; inputs are constructed so exactly one correct boolean result exists for each test case.

optimal.description: Decide whether pattern `p` matches string `s` using dynamic programming or recursion with memoization. Treat `*` as a modifier for the preceding element (zero or more occurrences) and `.` as a single-character wildcard. Both DP and memoized recursion run in O(|s| * |p|) time.

solution.approach: Use dynamic programming or recursion with memoization. For DP, build a table dp[i][j] meaning s[i:] matches p[j:], fill it bottom-up handling '*' as zero-or-more modifier and '.' as single-character wildcard. For recursion, memoize (i,j) results to avoid exponential branching. Both run in O(|s| * |p|) time.
solution.spaceComplexity: O(|s| * |p|) for full DP; O(|p|) with rolling 1D DP
